title: Restore Terminals config
description: Configuration for the Restore Terminals extension, at .vscode/restore-terminals.json. Any value set here wins over the equivalent restoreTerminals.* setting in settings.json.

runOnStartup.description: Whether or not to restore the terminals when VSCode starts up.

keepExistingTerminalsOpen.description: Whether or not to keep any currently open terminals open when restoring.

artificialDelayMilliseconds.description: Leave this out and Restore Terminals waits for each shell to actually start before running its commands. Set a number of milliseconds only if your setup still glitches out; it adds that pause between every step.

terminals.description: Each entry is one integrated terminal window.

cwd.description: The working directory for this terminal window and its splits. Supports ${workspaceFolder} in a single-root workspace and ${workspaceFolder:folderName} in a multi-root workspace.

location.description: Where this terminal window opens: "panel" for the terminal panel, or "editor" to open it as an editor tab. Its splits follow it either way. Leave it unset to use the terminal.integrated.defaultLocation setting.

splitTerminals.description: The terminals to split this window into, left to right.

name.description: The name to give the terminal.

icon.description: The id of a VSCode product icon, for example "terminal-bash" or "flame". See https://code.visualstudio.com/api/references/icons-in-labels for the full list.

color.description: The id of a VSCode theme colour for the terminal icon. The terminal.ansi* keys are recommended as they stay readable in every theme.

cwd.description: The working directory for this split only, overriding the terminal window's cwd. Supports the same ${workspaceFolder} variables.

shellPath.description: Path to a specific shell executable to run this split under, instead of the default terminal shell.

shellArgs.description: Arguments to pass to the shell executable.

env.description: Environment variables for this split, added to the ones it would normally inherit. Set a value to null to remove that variable.

commands.description: The shell commands to execute when this terminal opens.

shouldRunCommands.description: Whether to actually run the commands in the terminal, or just paste them there.
